risks: Hole round trip already wrong on main: a 100x100 lot with a 20x20 hole imported and exported through build/release/bin/katana_cli.exe came back as 2 polygons totalling 10400 m2 (true 9600). Nothing reads source.ring and export.cpp:200 writes every closed polyline as a polygon. Every overlay, dissolve or buffer built on the current conversion would inherit this, so the bridge must assemble only tagged rings; closed polylines nested in CAD are not holes.

Typed attributes are lost: import makes every attribute a string (gdal_adapter.hpp:109 map<string,string>; area_m2 8400.5 exported as String). SQL numeric filters and aggregates quietly compare text until P0 adds typed fields.

EXPORT writes no CRS even when the project has one: no caller sets VectorExportOptions::projectionWkt. docs/cad.md:249 also says GIS imports reproject into the project CRS, which the code does not do (only gis_online.cpp:513 sets targetCrs).

GDAL's algorithm framework is 'provisionally provided' (gdal CLI warning) and MSYS2 is a rolling release: algorithm names and arguments can change. Bind every path and argument in one table, and add a registry test that fails the build when one disappears.

API traps reproduced: Instantiate({"vector","pipeline"}) picks Instantiate(const std::string&) through the string's iterator-pair constructor (std::length_error / undefined behaviour), so always pass std::vector<std::string>. Writing dataset values into an argument in place leaves it unset ('Required argument input has not been specified'), so use GDALAlgorithmArg::Set(...).

Arbitrary code execution: the pipeline 'external' step runs any program once --config GDAL_ENABLE_EXTERNAL=YES is given (reproduced with cmd /c echo). A generic toolbox reachable by MCP must refuse --config, external, gdal vsi, dataset delete/rename/copy, and untrusted .gdalg.json files, which run pipelines when opened.

Semantics that surprise: gdal vector dissolve does NOT group by attribute (it needs combine --group-by first and yields GEOMETRYCOLLECTION); check-coverage refuses any non-polygon feature; clean-coverage closes only enclosed gaps; buffer output is 2D.
Heights: GDAL reads a 2D point as z=0. Grid, rasterize --3d and 3D clip over heightless entities would reproduce audit IO-01 (flat at the datum) unless the bridge excludes and counts them.

Curves: GEOS is linear. Arcs and circles are tessellated, and GDAL's default of 8 segments per quadrant gives a 0.096 m sagitta on a 5 m radius. Derive quadrant-segments from curveTolerance, and emit exact Circle entities for round point buffers.
Entity identity: LabelGeometry::target and associative dimensions refer to entity ids, so replacing entities in in-place operations would orphan lot-area labels. Use setEntityGeometry and keep ids.
Legal cadastre: clean-coverage, make-valid and snapping move boundaries. They must be report-first, with an explicit REPLACE and a warning, and never run silently on surveyed boundaries.

Reprojection accuracy: PROJ here has no GDA94-GDA2020 grid ('at least one grid missing') and falls back to the 7-parameter operation. A LOCAL import's originShift is not recorded (audit QT-07), so reprojecting or writing a CRS on shifted data would be wrong without that fix.

Layering: interop may not see cad, so it cannot parse scope clauses or read a Document. The executor belongs in katana_app with the window linking katana_app (allowed by the table, but a new link); otherwise it gets duplicated the way IMPORT/EXPORT already are (session.cpp:776, main_window.cpp:2052).

Dependency on unfinished work: scope_verbs.hpp and ScopeFilterWidget are not yet on main (none in the uscope-core worktree). OVERLAY and CLIP need a clause-level parse API added to the SHARED parser, so the lanes must wait for utility-scope or coordinate with it; a second parser is forbidden.

Scale and threading: MEM datasets are all in RAM and Spatialite over MEM has no spatial index, so large inputs need materialize to a temp GPKG. GDALDataset is not thread-safe: build plain feature tables on the GUI thread, and build the MEM dataset and run the algorithm inside the job, cancelling through the progress callback.

Field names: property keys like 12d.x or source.file need quoting in SQL; shapefile truncates field names to 10 characters on export; a property with mixed types across entities must become a String field, with a warning.

plan.summary:
Plan for the GDAL build swarm: one foundation package (F0) and 22 lane packages in 8 lanes, each lane in its own worktree. The work puts GDAL 3.13's algorithm framework, its drivers and its dataset tools on all three surfaces (window, katana_cli, katana_mcp).

**F0, the foundation**
- **The bridge (katana_io).** Plain types over GDAL's C++ algorithm registry: the catalogue, argument specs, and runs with progress and cancel.
- **The bindings (katana_interop).** Drawing data, surfaces, reference rasters and files go in. Results come back as reference rasters, entities (one undo step, on a target layer) or files.
- **One shared executor (katana_app).** It runs in three phases: prepare on the calling thread, work on a worker, apply as one undo step. katana_cli, katana_mcp and the window all run it; the window gains a link to katana_app for this.
- **The GDAL verb.** It takes GDAL's own command line, plus Katana FROM and TO clauses. FROM binds drawing data through the shared scope and filter.
- **Three MCP tools.** Catalogue, describe (with JSON argument schemas) and run.

**The lanes then add:**
- **Toolbox:** the GIS > GDAL Toolbox window, with its forms generated from the argument metadata.
- **Terrain:** a shared store of named surfaces with SURFACE verbs, then these tools, each with results in the drawing: contours, terrain shading, slope classes, statistics by area, drape and sample, viewshed and line of sight, gridding points to a DEM, and DEM tools.
- **Vector:** buffer, dissolve, overlay, hull, clip, check/repair/coverage, and SQL.
- **Files and formats:**
  - IMPORT, EXPORT, INFO, REFS and COPC move into one shared executor.
  - The silent data loss the investigators reproduced is fixed: no CRS written, KML and CSV losing geometry, MapInfo TAB quantising coordinates, holes and typed attributes lost.
  - Every driver and /vsi path is opened.
  - IMPORT and EXPORT gain options, and EXPORT takes the shared scope.
  - INFO replies with structured data, and reference layers can be managed and are saved with the project.

**Before F0 branches**, ui-gaps-build (P1's runVerbLine and CommandRunner) and utility-scope (scope_verbs.hpp, ScopeFilterWidget) must both be merged to main and green.

**The critical path** is F0, then I1 and I2 in parallel with I0, then I3, then I4. The terrain-b lane's T4 and T5 wait for T0.

## 2. The bridge (`katana::gis::processing`)

It wraps GDAL 3.13's C++ algorithm API behind the types in the contract. Every rule below was observed in the investigators' probes (`C:/GitHubProjects/Katana-wt/gdal-scratch/`).

**Catalogue**
- Walk the registry from `Instantiate("gdal")` through `GetSubAlgorithmNames()`. `GetNames()` misses the `driver` family.
- The result is cached with `std::call_once`: 121 leaf algorithms and 17 containers.

**Describing arguments**
- Read each `GDALAlgorithmArg` into an `ArgSpec`.
- Drop any argument where `IsHidden() || IsHiddenForAPI()` is true.
- A NaN min or max means there is no bound. Do not use the inclusive flag to decide that: 19 of the 82 minimums are exclusive.
- Split aliases into public and hidden at `HIDDEN_ALIAS_SEPARATOR`.
- `usageJson` is `GetUsageAsJSON()` verbatim.

**Running**
- Use a fresh instance for every run: `Run()` is single-shot.
- Instantiate with `std::vector<std::string>{...}`. A braced list binds to the string's iterator-pair constructor, which is undefined behaviour.
- Use `GetArg()` and check it for null. Never use `operator[]`, which hands back a dummy argument.
- **Binding inputs:**
  - Each `RasterGrid` or `FeatureSet` becomes its OWN MEM dataset, built inside `run()` on the worker thread. One shared MEM input gave 63 wrong results out of 120.
  - A dataset list is set with `Set(std::vector<GDALArgDatasetValue>&&)`. Writing into the list in place does not mark the argument as set.
  - Arguments that accept names only are staged under `/vsimem/katana/<uuid>/` and unlinked afterwards. These are `raster calc` inputs, the index inputs, and the outputs of `vector grid *`, `convert` and `raster pixel-info`.
- **Tokens:** GDAL-CLI tokens go to `ParseCommandLineArguments` AFTER the datasets are bound, so list, CRS and choice parsing is exactly GDAL's own.
- **Outputs:**
  - Memory: `--output-format MEM` with an empty output name.
  - REFERENCE: a tiled GTiff, `COMPRESS=DEFLATE`, with `PREDICTOR=3` for floating-point data.
  - FILE: the user's path.
  - Take the output reference BEFORE `Finalize()`.
  - A raster output larger than `maxMemoryCells` goes to a file and never into a `std::vector`.
- **Errors:**
  - Each run collects errors with a thread-local `CPLPushErrorHandlerEx`.
  - The process-wide `CPLQuietErrorHandler` stays: errors raised on GDAL's own worker threads (viewshed's, for example) reach only the global handler. Never install a per-run global handler.
  - The `Result` message is GDAL's first `CE_Failure`, which already carries the algorithm's prefix. `CE_Warning`s become `Diagnostic`s.
- **Cancel:**
  - The progress adapter maps the stop token to returning FALSE and records that it did.
  - The run counts as cancelled whenever that happened or a stop was requested, WHATEVER `Run()` returned. `raster hillshade` returns true after a cancel, with a partial output.
  - Outputs are then discarded and "User terminated" diagnostics dropped. The result is `InvalidState` "cancelled".
- **Config:**
  - Only an allow-list of thread-local options is accepted (`GDAL_NUM_THREADS`, `GDAL_CACHEMAX`).
  - `--config` is refused, and `GDAL_ENABLE_EXTERNAL` is never set.
  - Thread-local options do not reach GDAL's own threads, so nothing correctness-critical may depend on them.
- **Sidecars:** no `.aux.xml` may appear beside a user's file.
  - F0 chooses between a process-wide `GDAL_PAM_PROXY_DIR` in the cache and a thread-local `GDAL_PAM_ENABLED=NO` for runs. The choice depends on whether reading existing sidecars survives it, and F0 records the choice.
  - A test asserts that no new file appears beside a fixture after `raster info --stats`.

## 3. Bindings (`katana::interop::geo`)

**Drawing to FeatureSet** (`drawingDataset`, the ONE conversion; I1 moves `importVector` and `exportVector` onto it):
- **Tables:** `points`, `lines` and `polygons`. An empty table is omitted.
- **Fields:**
  - first `katana_id` (Integer64, the key that joins results back), then `layer`, `style`, `colour` and `type`;
  - then the properties, typed and sorted by key. A key whose type varies between entities becomes a String, with a warning.
- **Areas and holes:**
  - A closed polyline, or a circle, is an area (`closedAsPolygons`).
  - Nested closed polylines are NOT holes: a building inside a lot is not a hole in the lot.
  - Only rings tagged `source.ring=hole` or `gis.ring=hole` join their exterior. `gis.part=<n>` links them, and where it is absent GEOS organisePolygons decides.
- **Curves:** arcs and circles are linearised at `curveTolerance` (a 1 mm sagitta, the export's rule).
- **Heights:**
  - Z is written only when every vertex has a height (absent is not zero).
  - With `requireHeights` (grid, `rasterize --3d`), heightless entities are excluded and counted.
- **Other entities:** text, blocks and anything else unsupported are skipped and counted by reason.
- **CRS:** the project CRS is set on every table.

**Results to the drawing** (`resultCommand`): one `commands::Transaction` whose name is the verb line.
- **Create:** `createLayer` for any missing layer, then `createEntities`.
  - Several output tables go to `<layer>/<table>`.
  - Properties come from typed fields, plus `gis.op=<algorithm>` and `gis.source=<katana_id>` when a result carries one.
  - Polygon holes are tagged with `gis.ring` and `gis.part`.
  - No derived measure properties are written (area, length), because they go stale when the entity is edited. Replies carry the measures instead.
- **UpdateGeometry:** `setEntityGeometry` per `katana_id`. Ids are kept, so labels and associativity survive.
- **SetProperties:** `setEntityProperty` per `katana_id`.
- **Deleting sources:** `deleteEntities` only when REPLACE is asked.

**Rasters**
- `RASTER <id|name>` binds the reference raster's `source` path, read at full precision, never its RGBA copy.
- `SURFACE <name> [CELL m]` becomes `interop::geo::surfaceGrid`: the TIN sampled at cell centres, at `CELL` or `suggestedCellSize`, capped at 25M cells.
- `FILE` binds by name. `/vsi*` paths and URLs pass through untouched.

**Derived rasters**
- They go to `<project>/cache/gdal/<name>.tif`, or to the session's scratch directory when the drawing has no project (the reply then says `persisted=no`).
- They are imported with `interop::importRaster` as a `RasterOverlay` with `role=Derived` and `derivation` set to the verb line.

## 4. The executor (`katana::app::geo`)

**Three phases**, so that a session runs a line inline while the window runs it as a job:
1. **`prepare(Context&, line)`, on the calling or GUI thread.**
   - Tokenise with the interpreter's tokenizer.
   - Look up the verb table.
   - Resolve the algorithm and check its policy.
   - Parse FROM and TO with the ONE source parser and the ONE target parser.
   - Resolve scopes with `scope_verbs.hpp` and `cad::matchEntities` (VIEW goes through the interpreter's provider).
   - COPY everything the work needs (a FeatureSet, a grid, paths), plus copies of the entities an in-place apply will change.
   - Return a `Prepared`. Its `reply` is set for LIST, HELP, VERSION and PREVIEW, which have nothing to run.
2. **`work(stop, progress)`, on a worker or inline.** Pure: `processing::run()` and conversions only, never the Document or ReferenceData. It returns an `Apply`.
3. **`apply(Context&)`, on the calling or GUI thread.**
   - It executes ONE command, adds reference rasters and surfaces, and returns the reply records.
   - An in-place apply first compares its targets with the copies taken at prepare. If they differ, it refuses with `InvalidState` "the drawing changed while the job ran".

**How each front end reaches it**
- **katana_cli and katana_mcp.**
  - `Session::run` calls `geo::handles(line)`, then `geo::runNow`.
  - Records go to stdout; `error: <Code>: <message>` goes to stderr.
  - MCP tools build a line, run it through the Session, and parse the records into `structuredContent`.
  - `katana_gdal_catalogue` and `katana_gdal_describe` read the schema functions directly, since they are read-only.
- **The window.**
  - A typed line, or a dialog's line through `runVerbLine`, reaches `runWorkbenchLine`, then `GeoWorkbench::runLine`, then prepare on the GUI thread.
  - An immediate reply is logged at once.
  - Otherwise `JobRunner::start(title, work)` runs it, with status-bar progress and Cancel. The job's Apply calls the executor's apply and logs the records.
  - Headless runs (`--command`, `--run-line`, scripts) call `JobRunner::waitFor`, so they are synchronous and their outcomes testable.
  - Interactively, `runVerbLine` returns the record `job id=<n> title="..." state=started`. When the job ends, the workbench calls `GeoServices::finished(JobId, VerbOutcome)`, and that is how dialogs show the result.

**Verb table and helpers**
- The verb table (`geo/verb_table.cpp`) maps a verb, plus an optional second word, to a prepare function and its usage text.
- `helpText()` is built from the table, so HELP, the window's Command Reference and `katana_help` agree.
- Curated verbs are thin modules on the same helpers: `parseSource`, `parseTarget`, `bindDrawing`, `bindRaster`, `applyOutputs`, `scopeRecord`. Each builds one or more `RunRequest`s and chooses a `ResultMode`.

## 5. Safety policy

- **Classification:** every leaf is Safe or Confirm.
  - A curated table decides, backed by a rule: an input dataset argument carrying the UPDATE flag makes an algorithm Confirm.
  - The `vsi` writers are Confirm: delete, move, sync, copy and sozip.
  - So are `dataset delete`, `rename` and `copy`, `driver * repack`, `raster overview add|delete|refresh`, `raster edit` (in place), and `raster update` / `vector update`.
  - An unclassified leaf is Confirm, and the contract test lists every unclassified leaf.
- **Confirm algorithms** need `CONFIRM` in the line, the toolbox's Confirm box, or `confirm:true` in MCP.
- **Refused outright:** pipeline `external` steps, `--config`, `--help`, `--json-usage` and `--progress` tokens. `SPATIALITE_SECURITY` is never set, so Spatialite's file functions stay disabled.
- **Existing files:** TO FILE never replaces a file without `OVERWRITE`. Katana never writes beside a user's input.
- **MCP:** `katana_gdal_run` carries `destructiveHint` and `openWorldHint`, since URLs are accepted.

## 6. Errors (`core::Status` / `Result`)

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `InvalidArgument` | Grammar; an unknown argument (named); a value GDAL refused (GDAL's message); validation (required, exclusion, dependency); GDAL tokens after a clause |
| `NotFound` | An algorithm, layer, reference raster, surface or file |
| `Unsupported` | A Confirm algorithm without CONFIRM; a target the output kind cannot go to (a vector into REFERENCE) |
| `InvalidState` | "cancelled"; "the drawing changed while the job ran" |
| `FileImportFailure` / `FileExportFailure` | GDAL could not open an input / could not write an output |
| `CommandRejected` | GDAL ran and failed; the context is GDAL's first failure message |
| `InvalidCRS` | Only where a curated tool refuses mismatched CRSs |

A scope that matches nothing is not an error: it is reported with `matched=0`.

notDoing: Lazy 'stream' outputs as previews: the lazy dataset is not thread-safe and keeps its inputs alive after the run. PREVIEW validates the arguments and reports what the scope took instead.

GDALG (.gdalg.json) files as Katana's recipe format: Serialize() cannot write inputs bound as objects ('<input:unserialisable>'). A .kcs script replays any GDAL line together with its drawing bindings. Opening someone else's .gdalg.json still works as a FILE source, because GDALG is a driver.

Free-form raster algebra through raster calc: this MSYS2 GDAL has neither muparser nor ExprTk, so only the builtin functions work (sum, mean, min, max, diff). The toolbox exposes calc and says so. RASTER DIFFERENCE uses the builtin diff.

A bridge built on the C API only: the same toolchain builds Katana and GDAL, and only the C++ API gives the bounds (min/max with inclusivity) that the forms and JSON Schemas need. A move to an MSVC-built GDAL would need the C API plus the usage JSON; that is recorded in docs/geoprocessing.md, not built.

Naming the verb PROCESS rather than GDAL: the argument vocabulary is GDAL's own, which agents already know from the gdal command line, and the GIS menu already names its sections after GDAL. The naming rule covers other names, not this one.

Native tools for algorithms Katana already does exactly (convex hull, simplify, offset) or that no survey or civil task needs: tpi, tri, roughness, proximity, as-features, clean-collar, rgb-to-palette, pansharpen, tile, set-type/scale/unscale/select/stack, create, compare, resize, mdim mosaic, and vector sort/swap-xy/rename-layer/edit/concat/index/export-schema/simplify-coverage/partition. All of these are reachable through the GDAL verb and the toolbox.

A native UI for destructive file operations (vsi delete/move/sync/copy/sozip, dataset delete/rename/copy, driver repack, overview delete, raster edit in place): these stay in the GDAL verb and the toolbox behind CONFIRM, and in MCP only with confirm:true.

Reprojecting the drawing in place (a datum change of entities, with arcs refitted and text rotated by grid convergence): that is geodesy work, not an algorithm wrapper, and vector reproject would tessellate the arcs and drop the text. Files are reprojected on import and export instead (I3, I4).

ONLINE on katana_cli/katana_mcp, and retrofitting its area= grammar to the shared scope: the scope-retrofit list from utility-scope's audit owns ONLINE's second scope grammar, and this is not algorithm integration. It is to be recorded under 'Not done' in docs/gis_online.md if it is not already there.
Re-reading reference rasters at view resolution so they stay sharp at every zoom: that is a change to plan-view rendering. D2 only builds overviews on request.

Saving surfaces in the project file: that is a storage-schema decision of its own. T0's store is session data, as reference data is today. D2 persists reference-raster sources, which covers derived rasters.
Reading with GetArrowStream in bulk: no measurement shows that reading vector features is the bottleneck (CLAUDE.md section 5 says measure first).
Widgets for each driver's options: option lists come from the driver registry (FORMATS, INFO) and are entered as KEY=VALUE rows.
Per-run global error handlers or global config options: they are unsafe with concurrent runs, because errors raised on GDAL's worker threads reach only the global handler.
A raster height readout in the ID Point inquiry tool: that is a change to a cad tool. RASTER SAMPLE and DRAPE cover the need; the readout is a follow-up.
Using a GDAL concave hull as the boundary for SURFACE FROM DRAWING inside this swarm: it crosses two lanes (V3 and T0), so it is a small follow-up once both are on main.
New icons for every tool: no lane edits icons.*. Lanes reuse existing icons or F0's generic Icon::Processing, and a set of icons is a later design pass.
risks: The algorithm framework is provisional (gdal --help reserves the right to rename and reorganise it), 3.13 already changed raster inputs to dataset_list, and MSYS2 upgrades GDAL on a rolling basis. Mitigation: every form, schema and HELP comes from metadata read at run time, and every package pins the paths and arguments it binds in a contract test that names what changed.

Run()'s return value cannot be trusted after a cancel. hillshade returns true with a partial output; slope, aspect, roughness, tpi and contour fail with no message; vector algorithms report a misleading 'Failed to write layer'. Mitigation: the progress adapter tracks cancel itself, outputs are discarded, and tests cover it. Pipelines and vector algorithms report progress once, so cancelling them is best-effort, and the UI must say that they stop at the end.

Errors raised on GDAL's own worker threads (viewshed's, for example) skip the thread-local collector. The global CPLQuietErrorHandler must stay, and a test must show that the propagated failure still reaches the Status.

Datasets shared between concurrent runs give wrong results (63 of 120). Each run owns its MEM datasets and opens RASTER sources by path itself. Any later optimisation that shares a dataset must use GDALGetThreadSafeDataset, and must prove its results identical to the unshared run.
Thread-local config options do not reach threads GDAL spawns. Nothing correctness-critical may depend on them, and the way sidecar files are prevented must be verified by a test, not assumed.

Memory: big raster outputs, surface grids and FeatureSets with millions of features. Rasters spill to files above maxMemoryCells, surface grids are capped at 25M cells, and the cost of creating entities in an apply is measured (benchmarks/bench_geo_apply.cpp) before anything is promised for large results.

The drawing may change while a job runs. Create-only applies are safe. In-place modes (REPAIR, CLIP REPLACE, SetProperties, DRAPE) compare their targets with the copies taken at prepare and refuse when they differ; a wrong comparison would silently overwrite a concurrent edit.

Preconditions drift. The names in scope_verbs.hpp are unknown until utility-scope merges, and V2/V3 need a clause-level entry point with stop words. F0 adapts to what exists and extends the shared parser rather than writing a second one. If ui-gaps-build is not merged, F0's hotspot edits to dispatchLine and runVerbLine have nothing to attach to.

Hotspot conflicts across 8 lanes. The mitigations are the globbed directories, the reserved blocks, the gis_dialogs split and the one-file-per-verb split. main_window.cpp is still touched by F0, T0, I0, I2 and D2; the integrator merges in priority order and runs the whole suite after each merge.

Build load: nine worktrees, each needing a full first build on one machine. Cap each at -j 4 and let at most five build at once, or the lanes starve each other and hit the 10-minute tool limit (which moves a build to the background and risks two ninjas in one directory).

I0 changes the reply format of IMPORT/EXPORT/INFO/REFS from prose to key=value records. That breaks existing cli.* regexes and anyone scripting against the prose. It must be treated as a documented change of specification, with the reason stated in the commit, and never as expectations edited to match output.

Agent safety. Spatialite's file functions are enabled if SPATIALITE_SECURITY=relaxed is ever set. A pipeline 'external' step runs programs if GDAL_ENABLE_EXTERNAL is set, and --config would set it. /vsicurl and URL sources reach the network. Katana refuses the tokens and never sets either option; tests assert both refusals, and no test uses the network.

CRS: the drawing may have no CRS, or hold data imported LOCAL (shifted; audit QT-07), so GDAL results will not register against georeferenced rasters. Replies warn when the CRSs differ, and the curated raster tools refuse when both are known and differ. Imported .prj/WKT naming differs from EPSG definitions, so equivalence must be judged with OGRSpatialReference::IsSame, not by comparing text.

Z is lost: buffer and most vector algorithms output 2D, and a heightless entity given to a Z-consuming algorithm would be read as z = 0 (the IO-01 failure again). Such entities are excluded and counted, and replies say when results are 2D.

Precision: GDAL writes some outputs as Float32 (slope, aspect, contours at 9.99998 against an exact 10). Tests must state their tolerance with the error analysis behind it, and never loosen it to fit.

Linking katana_app into the window makes the link larger and brings session.cpp's internals into the same binary as the window's. Symbols must stay in anonymous namespaces, the release link time must be checked, and mcp_server objects must be pulled in only through what is referenced.

The hand-worked shadow edge in the viewshed and line-of-sight tests depends on GDAL's curvature and target-height conventions. The test fixture must switch curvature off (curvature=none) so that the similar-triangles value is the true expectation.
